s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations and syncope in a patient with complex congenital heart disease
salient_findings: Tachycardia with heart rate of 183 bpm
Irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating on ECG
key_facts: Patient has complex congenital heart disease
Patient has D-transposition of the great arteries
Patient has single ventricle physiology
Patient has Fontan circulation
Patient experiences lightheadedness and syncope while walking
Patient has been prescribed diltiazem and apixaban
ECG shows irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating
Transesophageal echocardiogram shows no intracardiac thrombus
Patient has persistent tachycardia and palpitations despite initial treatment

shortlist.label: Intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG shows irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating and intermittently visible P waves, which is consistent with intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia (IART), particularly in the context of the patient's complex congenital heart disease and Fontan circulation.

rejected.label: Atrial fibrillation
rejected.why: Atrial fibrillation typically presents with a completely irregular rhythm, whereas the patient's ECG shows grouped beating, suggesting a more organized arrhythmia.

rejected.label: Atrial flutter
rejected.why: Atrial flutter typically presents with a regular, rapid atrial rhythm, which is not consistent with the patient's irregularly irregular tachycardia.

rejected.label: Supraventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: Supraventricular tachycardia is a broad term that encompasses several types of arrhythmias, but the patient's ECG and clinical presentation suggest a more specific diagnosis of intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia.

rejected.label: Focal atrial tachycardia
rejected.why: Focal atrial tachycardia typically presents with a regular, monomorphic P wave morphology, which is not consistent with the patient's ECG showing grouped beating and intermittently visible P waves.
